stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Apple devices.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating active development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring that processing occurs entirely on the user's own device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries derived from RGB videos.
Utilizes novel Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to embed high-level geometric priors into the VLM architecture.

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces GraphVid, a new method for controllable video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current methods in precisely controlling complex, multi-object interactions in video.
Uses a graph-based approach to enable flexible and precise control over multiple subjects, overcoming issues with trajectory drawing and occlusion.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
Enables the training of harness-native agents across diverse and complex environments.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries learned from RGB videos.
Employs Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to enhance the 3D spatial awareness capabilities of existing VLMs.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in deep logical reasoning capabilities of large audio-language models compared to text-based LLMs.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework to transfer reasoning from a text teacher to an audio student.
The method tackles data scarcity by leveraging existing powerful text models to enhance audio model reasoning.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models specifically for African languages.
The models utilize the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder and cover 27 language varieties across several African nations.
Training data primarily consists of read speech sourced from religious texts, ensuring broad and license-clear usage.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical performance bottleneck in speculative decoding when using Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) heads with very long contexts (millions of tokens).
The core issue is that the MTP draft head's attention mechanism scales linearly with the entire KV cache, making the draft generation cost prohibitive at large contexts.
The proposed solution, Windowed-MTP, aims to mitigate this 'full-context draft-KV tax' to maintain efficiency in frontier models operating at massive context lengths.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search functionality in Claude Code.
This enhancement suggests deeper integration of advanced AI capabilities (like multi-step reasoning and external data retrieval) into local LLM environments.

stories.title: After backlash, Meta pauses plan to ‘rate limit’ its smart glasses
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has paused its plan to introduce a $20 monthly subscription fee for a feature on its smart glasses.
The feature in question allows users to hear each other more clearly and operates locally on the device.
The pause comes following public backlash against the proposed monetization strategy.

stories.title: SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after auspicious end to 13th flight
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX plans to attempt a 'tower catch' for the next Starship flight.
This maneuver follows the recent conclusion of the 13th Starship flight.
The focus remains on improving Starship's recovery and operational success.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major social media platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are accused of obstructing data access.
Researchers claim the tech giants are failing to comply with legal data provision requirements.
The issue highlights ongoing tensions between Big Tech and European regulatory/research bodies.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update is characterized by token efficiency improvements rather than a massive jump in core capabilities.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective AI models are often sufficient for practical applications.
This signals a trend where optimization and operational efficiency are becoming as important as raw performance gains in LLMs.

stories.title: Roku raises streaming stick prices by up to 60 percent
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Roku is significantly increasing the price of its streaming sticks by up to 60%.
The company attributes the price hike to a shortage of RAM.
The news contrasts with a positive outlook previously expressed by the CEO.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of simply reducing sycophancy in LLMs.
It proposes that socially calibrated models must learn to distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent moral judgment.
The study identifies three structured dimensions governing how LLMs revise their judgments based on external input.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study highlights that different views (text-only, diagram-only, combined) can elicit different behaviors in VLMs, even for equivalent problems.
The research proposes that these view-dependent inconsistencies suggest that different modalities expose complementary reasoning pathways.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across state spaces of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
The research aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
stories.author: Maxim Secor
bullet_points: Introduces EnsembleEGNN, a new foundation model for molecular property prediction that accounts for conformational ensembles.
The model uses Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNN) to encode individual conformers, followed by a Set Attention Block for pooling.
It is pre-trained on CREMP, a dataset specifically focused on cyclic peptide ensembles.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study highlights that different views (text, diagram, combined) can elicit different behaviors, suggesting complementary reasoning paths.
The research introduces 'MIRROR' to address this gap, aiming to improve multi-modal reasoning by learning from alternative perspectives.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that uses LLMs to transform static clinical cases into interactive, decision-centered learning games.
Addresses a limitation in current medical education AI by moving beyond simple Q&A to create structured, narrative learning trajectories.
Employs a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to ground the storytelling in clinical reality.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
It addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
The framework enables harness-native agents to be trained across diverse and complex environments.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research introduces GS-Agent, a method to generate dynamic and physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language descriptions.
Current generative methods struggle with ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in these complex simulations.
The work addresses the limitations of traditional computer graphics, which require extensive manual human effort.

stories.title: Artificial Epanorthosis: Why large language models overuse a classical rhetorical figure, and how to mitigate it
stories.author: Federico Boggia
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit systematic overuse of the rhetorical figure 'epanorthosis' (self-correction).
This overuse is attributed to training data rich in promotional prose and RLHF preferences for confident phrasing.
The analysis suggests the left-to-right generation process contributes to this rhetorical pattern.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent code concepts across different programming languages (Python and Rust).
It uses a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the specific task, the programming language, and the underlying model architecture on code representation.
The study measures a comprehensive inventory of grammatical concepts (58 for Python, 57 for Rust) to determine if representations are consistent across the tested configurations.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy constraint of using cloud-based LLMs for code development, especially with sensitive data.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as a viable alternative for data preparation tasks.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the performance of AI agents running in a local, cloud-free environment.

stories.title: DeepSeek pause fundraise after comments on compute gap to US leaked (transcript) [pdf]
stories.author: oliculipolicula
bullet_points: DeepSeek paused its fundraising efforts.
The pause was reportedly linked to comments made by the company regarding the compute gap relative to the US.
The news originated from a leaked transcript shared on Hacker News.

stories.title: Inflect-Micro-v2: complete voice in 9.36M parameters
stories.author: nateb2022
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Inflect-Micro-v2', a new voice model.
The model is notable for having 9.36 million parameters.
The announcement originates from Hacker News, suggesting a technical audience interest.

stories.title: Fail Closed, Not Open: Designing an AI Gateway for Regulated Enterprises
stories.author: abhijat_chaturvedi
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of routing LLM requests correctly across multiple enterprise teams.
Focuses on the concept of an 'AI Gateway' designed for regulated environments.
Highlights the need for robust control mechanisms ('Fail Closed') over LLM usage.

stories.title: AI Coding Isn't the Problem. AI Engineering Is.
stories.author: bayu911
bullet_points: The article argues that the core issue in AI development is not the coding itself.
It posits that 'AI Engineering' represents the true, more complex challenge in software development.
The piece suggests that software creation involves activities beyond just writing code.
